issues.description: The Windows bootstrap and update paths invoke PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) unconditionally, so they fail with program-not-found on systems that only have the Windows-bundled `powershell.exe`.
issues.rationale: At the selected head, `install_verusfmt`, `compile_verus`, and the Windows Z3 download path all construct `Command::new("pwsh")` without probing availability. A normal Windows installation may provide only `powershell.exe`; in that environment the child process cannot be spawned and bootstrap/update stops before the required script runs. PR #127's title and body report this exact `program not found` failure and state that both shells were tested. Repair commit 11116bf7ae9b5fe7b9e73be951a5b5ed4b8baab0 adds `get_powershell_command`, tries `pwsh`, and falls back to `powershell`. The PR #23 head entered mainline as patch-equivalent commit 2faf9a1ecefa763fcd9d17aecbeb951ee2996fdd, which is an ancestor of the repair.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Windows bootstrap and historical Verus were not executed. Primary and independent second reviewers inspected the complete four-commit PR history, fixed final diff, active call paths, patch-equivalent mainline ancestry, PR #127 author report, and repair commit.
